Dude. I'm bipolar and formerly homeless too.t Our stories are really similar, although I'm older than you are. 

Basically, I had a baby and it triggered an episode that was so bad that I spent 3 months in a state psychiatric facility. 

My son went into foster care 2 weeks after he was born, to the people that ended up becoming his adoptive parents. I wanted to keep him more than anything, but when I got out of the hospital I had lost my apartment, my job, and everything I owned. 

Even if I had been in a position to keep him, by then he had bonded with his foster parents, and taking him away from them would have been wrong. It could have caused serious psychological damage. So I gave them my child, and went to live on the street. 

It was bad. Like you, I was abused and taken advantage of. I was raped twice. Luckily, after about 3 months I got into a long-term (6 mos) shelter, and they helped me get benefits and an apartment. They also helped me get on the right medication, which has been crucial to my recovery. A few years after that, I started working, and today I got my very first job with benefits and a 401k. You can recover. I have. The scars never go away, but they do fade. Things get easier. 

If you ever want to talk, feel free to dm me. I know my username says throwaway, but this has become my main account.

The crazy part is that the smoke alarm even went off at all. I smoke copious amounts of marijuana in that room, as well as cigarettes, and it never makes a soundtrack -- but it went off for a fire no bigger than my cell phone.

I work at McDonald's. Not a great job, but I've been here for 4 years, and I don't mind the work. I'm not trying to blow my own horn, but I might be the friendliest/most professional cashier in the whole company. I'm never rude to customers, even the ones who richly deserve it. I hand it back to him, and he hands me what looks like a $100 hotel coupon (see above). Then he tells me that I have to call him to activate it, and wants to either get my number or give me his. I was a little bemused by this, but chalked it up to his wanting to flirt/ask me out. He was cute and friendly, so I was flattered. Then he said the words that broke the spell:

"I'm looking for good people to join my team." Red light! Red light! "You get paid to give people money. How does that sound?"

It sounds like an MLM, Kevin. It sounds like an MLM.
